newsitem.title: USA: MCI renames SHL unit, launches new service.
newsitem.headline: MCI renames SHL unit, launches new service.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp on Wednesday said it was renaming its SHL Systemhouse subsidiary MCI Systemhouse and said it expected the unit to exceed $1.4 billion in revenues in 1996.
MCI also said it launched a new outsourcing service networkMCI Enterprise Management, which would build, support and manage multiple computer networks for medium-sized companies across the country.
MCI bought the Canadian software company for $1 billion in November 1995. Since then it has been growing at twice the industry rate, MCI said.

"MCI Systemhouse combines the power of MCI's global brand name and network with the strong reputation and expertise of (SHL) Systemhouse in the global information technology marketplace," said Tim Price, chief operating officer of MCI's telecommunications subsidiary.
The new service is designed to give medium sized companies the level of support and network effectiveness previously only available to giant multinational corporations, MCI said.
SHL had revenues of C$1.2 billion in 1994, the last full year before its acquisition by MCI.

MCI said at the time of the $13-per share acquisition that the new company would add $1.5 billion to MCI revenues over four years but would dilute earnings in 1996 by four cents per share. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
